name: Keloid surgery + radiation

lead: The keloid is surgically removed, so the raised scar is gone right away, and the wound is then treated with radiation to keep it from growing back.

Wikipedia reports recurrence of 70 to 100 percent after excision alone, and lower recurrence when radiation, pressure therapy or laser is added. Published studies describe surgery plus radiotherapy as a standard approach for severe keloids, and one 2020 paper calls radiotherapy essential for preventing recurrence.

paras: Radiation is given in the days around the operation as a short course. Researchers also study add-ons such as steroid injection, hyperbaric oxygen, botulinum toxin, photobiomodulation and tension-reducing suturing.
Recurrence, sometimes larger than the original keloid, is the main documented problem. Wikipedia notes radiation is not recommended for children because of the risk of growth abnormalities.

angle.text: Surgical removal takes out the keloid at once, and radiation afterward lowers the chance it regrows, leaving a flat scar. It is a clinical standard for severe cases, since excision alone has high recurrence.

lead: Keloid excision with adjuvant radiation therapy is a combination in which a keloid is surgically removed and the wound is then treated with radiation to reduce regrowth. Wikipedia reports that excision alone has a recurrence rate of 70 to 100 percent, that recurrences can be larger, and that adding radiation, pressure therapy or laser sharply lowers recurrence; it adds that radiation is not recommended for children because of growth-abnormality risk [1].

Published studies describe surgery plus radiotherapy as a standard approach for severe keloids; one 2020 paper states that radiotherapy is essential for preventing recurrence [2]. Researchers also study adjuncts: hyperbaric oxygen, steroid injection, botulinum toxin, photobiomodulation and tension-reducing suturing [3][4][5][6][7].
Keloids most often affect people of sub-Saharan African, Asian or Latin American ancestry and commonly follow earlobe piercing [1].

paras: Excision removes the keloid tissue; adjuvant radiation, delivered as electron-beam, superficial or brachytherapy treatment, targets the wound bed afterwards. A 2023 study examined risk factors for recurrence after keloid surgery with electron radiotherapy [8], and a registered study followed high dose rate brachytherapy in 43 patients [9].

A 2020 report with geometric modelling and a retrospective cohort assessed superficial and deep fascia tensile reduction in severe keloid surgery, proposing that reduced skin tension helps outcomes [2]. A 1998 paper described reconstructing the earlobe with a subcutaneous island pedicle flap after earlobe keloid resection, noting that large earlobe keloids are hard to treat by non-surgical means [10].

A 2018 randomized study of 240 patients examined hyperbaric oxygen therapy after excision and radiotherapy for reducing recurrence [3]. A randomized trial studied immediate triamcinolone injection after auricular keloid surgery [4], and a 1994 report described steroid injection after surgery [11]. Botulinum toxin combined with superficial radiotherapy after chest keloid surgery was analysed in a 2025 paper [5], and a 2022 trial protocol proposed photobiomodulation with steroid injection around surgery, noting that no gold-standard treatment exists [6]. Registered trials include excision with steroid injection after caesarean (146 participants) [12], imiquimod (terminated) [13] and siRNA microneedle patches [14].

The studies above are mostly small trials, retrospective cohorts and protocols; abstracts reviewed for this article do not allow effect sizes to be summarised. A large registered retrospective study of keloid disorder planned 5,000 participants [15].
The topic arises mainly in discussions of piercing and scars. No forum material was available for this entry, so community claims are not documented.

timeline.event: A report describes intralesional steroid injection following keloid surgery. [11]
A subcutaneous island pedicle flap is described for earlobe reconstruction after keloid resection. [10]
A randomized study of hyperbaric oxygen after keloid surgery and radiotherapy is published. [3]
